ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, O is the center of the circumcircle of a regular N-gon (N is an even number greater than 3) with radius R. A point charge with charge amount +2q is placed at one vertex A of the regular N-gon, and point charges each with charge amount -q are placed at the remaining vertices respectively (not shown). Then what is the magnitude of the electric field strength at the center O?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a circle can be seen, with the position of the center marked as O inside the circle; there is a vertex A at the very top of the circumference, and at A a small circle with a “+” sign is drawn, indicating that a positive charge is placed at this vertex; from the figure it can be judged that A is on the circumference of the circumcircle, therefore AO is the circle radius R. The problem statement additionally explains that this is the circumcircle of a regular N-gon, A is one of its vertices, the point charge at A is +2q, and the charges at all the other vertices are -q. Reasoning: Decompose the actual charge distribution equivalently into two parts: the first part is to place -q at all N vertices of the regular N-gon; the second part is to additionally superpose +3q at point A. In this way the total charge at point A is -q+3q=+2q, and the remaining vertices are still -q, consistent with the original problem. For the first part, because the regular N-gon is symmetric about the center O, all vertices are at equal distances from O, and the electric field vectors cancel each other by symmetry, so the resultant electric field strength at point O is 0. Thus the electric field strength at point O comes only from the additional +3q at point A. The distance from A to O is R, and the magnitude of the electric field strength produced by a point charge at a distance R is E=k(3q)/R^2. Therefore the magnitude of the electric field strength at the center O is 3kq/R^2.
